question: Which airports have shipments marked delivered that were never actually handed over?

question: How much did we invoice each month in 2025, and what's the running total over the year?

question: Which 5 planes have the shortest average time on the ground between completed flights?
question_template: Which 5 planes have the shortest average time on the ground between completed flights?
answer_spec: Columns: tail_number, average ground time in hours between an aircraft's completed flight's actual arrival and its next completed flight's actual departure, rounded to 1 decimal; the 5 aircraft with the shortest average; ties by tail_number.
gold_sql: WITH s AS ( SELECT aircraft_id, actual_departure, LAG(actual_arrival) OVER (PARTITION BY aircraft_id ORDER BY actual_departure) AS prev_arrival FROM flights WHERE status = 'completed' ) SELECT a.tail_number, ROUND(AVG((julianday(s.actual_departure) - julianday(s.prev_arrival)) * 24), 1) AS avg_ground_hours FROM s JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = s.aircraft_id WHERE s.prev_arrival IS NOT NULL GROUP BY a.aircraft_id, a.tail_number ORDER BY avg_ground_hours ASC, a.tail_number LIMIT 5

gold_sql: WITH t AS ( SELECT f.origin_airport_id AS ap, SUM(s.total_weight_kg) / 1000.0 AS tonnes FROM flight_cargo fc JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id = fc.flight_id JOIN shipments s ON s.shipment_id = fc.shipment_id WHERE fc.leg_status = 'flown' GROUP BY f.origin_airport_id ), r AS (SELECT ap, tonnes, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY tonnes DESC) AS rnk FROM t) SELECT r.rnk AS tonnage_rank, a.iata_code, ROUND(r.tonnes, 1) AS tonnes FROM r JOIN airports a ON a.airport_id = r.ap WHERE r.rnk <= 5 ORDER BY r.rnk, a.iata_code

question: For each plane model, how many completed flights were more than half full by volume?
question_template: For each plane model, how many completed flights were more than half full by volume?
answer_spec: Columns: model, number of completed flights whose loaded volume (sum of shipment total_volume_m3) exceeded 50% of the type's max_volume_m3; models with none omitted; ordered by model.
gold_sql: WITH v AS ( SELECT fc.flight_id, SUM(s.total_volume_m3) AS m3 FROM flight_cargo fc JOIN shipments s ON s.shipment_id = fc.shipment_id GROUP BY fc.flight_id ) SELECT t.model, COUNT(*) AS half_full_flights FROM v JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id = v.flight_id AND f.status = 'completed' JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = f.aircraft_id JOIN aircraft_types t ON t.type_id = a.type_id WHERE v.m3 > 0.5 * t.max_volume_m3 GROUP BY t.type_id, t.model ORDER BY t.model

question: Which 3 warehouses keep delivered goods the longest between arriving from the flight and handing them over?
question_template: Which 3 warehouses keep delivered goods the longest between arriving from the flight and handing them over?
answer_spec: Columns: warehouse_code, delivered shipments, average hours between the RCF and DLV events of the same shipment at that warehouse (rounded 2); warehouses with at least 20 such shipments; the 3 with the longest average.
gold_sql: SELECT w.warehouse_code, COUNT(*) AS deliveries, ROUND(AVG((julianday(d.event_time) - julianday(r.event_time)) * 24), 2) AS avg_dwell_hours FROM tracking_events r JOIN tracking_events d ON d.shipment_id = r.shipment_id AND d.event_code = 'DLV' JOIN warehouses w ON w.warehouse_id = r.warehouse_id WHERE r.event_code = 'RCF' GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.warehouse_code HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20 ORDER BY avg_dwell_hours DESC, w.warehouse_code LIMIT 3

question: At which 5 airports do shipments wait the longest between being dropped off and flying out?
question_template: At which 5 airports do shipments wait the longest between being dropped off and flying out?
answer_spec: Columns: origin iata_code, average hours between a shipment's RCS scan and its first DEP event (rounded 2); shipments that departed only; the 5 airports with the longest average.
gold_sql: WITH t AS ( SELECT shipment_id, MIN(CASE WHEN event_code = 'RCS' THEN event_time END) AS rcs, MIN(CASE WHEN event_code = 'DEP' THEN event_time END) AS dep FROM tracking_events GROUP BY shipment_id ) SELECT a.iata_code, ROUND(AVG((julianday(t.dep) - julianday(t.rcs)) * 24), 2) AS avg_hours_rcs_to_departure FROM t JOIN shipments s ON s.shipment_id = t.shipment_id JOIN airports a ON a.airport_id = s.origin_airport_id WHERE t.rcs IS NOT NULL AND t.dep IS NOT NULL GROUP BY a.airport_id, a.iata_code ORDER BY avg_hours_rcs_to_departure DESC, a.iata_code LIMIT 5

question: For each plane model, what was the single most expensive finished maintenance job?
question_template: For each plane model, what was the single most expensive finished maintenance job?
answer_spec: Columns: model, work_order_number, cost (parts + labour, rounded 2): per aircraft model the most expensive completed maintenance record; ordered by model.
gold_sql: WITH m AS ( SELECT t.model, r.work_order_number, r.parts_cost_usd + r.labor_cost_usd AS cost, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.type_id ORDER BY r.parts_cost_usd + r.labor_cost_usd DESC, r.work_order_number) AS rn FROM maintenance_records r JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = r.aircraft_id JOIN aircraft_types t ON t.type_id = a.type_id WHERE r.status = 'completed' ) SELECT model, work_order_number, ROUND(cost, 2) AS cost_usd FROM m WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY model

question: For each airline, what percentage of completed flights left more than 15 minutes late?
question_template: For each airline, what percentage of completed flights left more than 15 minutes late?
answer_spec: Columns: airline name, completed flights, percentage departing more than 15 minutes late (rounded 1); ordered by percentage DESC.
gold_sql: SELECT al.name AS airline_name, COUNT(*) AS completed_flights, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN (julianday(f.actual_departure) - julianday(f.scheduled_departure)) * 1440 > 15 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS late_departure_pct FROM flights f JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = f.aircraft_id JOIN airlines al ON al.airline_id = a.airline_id WHERE f.status = 'completed' GROUP BY al.airline_id, al.name ORDER BY late_departure_pct DESC, airline_name

question: At which connecting airports did two-leg shipments sit more than 48 hours between flights?
question_template: At which connecting airports did two-leg shipments sit more than 48 hours between flights?
answer_spec: Columns: connecting airport iata_code, number of two-leg shipments whose ground time there (leg 2 actual departure - leg 1 actual arrival) exceeded 48 hours; both legs flown; ordered by count DESC, iata_code.
gold_sql: SELECT a.iata_code, COUNT(*) AS long_connections FROM flight_cargo l1 JOIN flight_cargo l2 ON l2.shipment_id = l1.shipment_id AND l2.leg_number = 2 JOIN flights f1 ON f1.flight_id = l1.flight_id JOIN flights f2 ON f2.flight_id = l2.flight_id JOIN airports a ON a.airport_id = f1.destination_airport_id WHERE l1.leg_number = 1 AND f1.status = 'completed' AND f2.status = 'completed' AND (julianday(f2.actual_departure) - julianday(f1.actual_arrival)) * 24 > 48 GROUP BY a.airport_id, a.iata_code ORDER BY long_connections DESC, a.iata_code

question: Which captain and first officer pairs flew together on at least 10 completed flights?
question_template: Which captain and first officer pairs flew together on at least 10 completed flights?
answer_spec: Columns: captain employee_number, first officer employee_number, completed flights flown together (captain + first_officer roles on the same flight); pairs with at least 10 flights together; ordered by count DESC, captain, first officer.
gold_sql: SELECT mc.employee_number AS captain, mf.employee_number AS first_officer, COUNT(*) AS flights_together FROM crew_assignments c JOIN crew_assignments fo ON fo.flight_id = c.flight_id AND fo.duty_role = 'first_officer' JOIN crew_members mc ON mc.crew_member_id = c.crew_member_id JOIN crew_members mf ON mf.crew_member_id = fo.crew_member_id WHERE c.duty_role = 'captain' AND c.assignment_status = 'completed' GROUP BY mc.employee_number, mf.employee_number HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10 ORDER BY flights_together DESC, captain, first_officer

question: Which customers still have open invoices but haven't paid anything in the last 60 days, and how many invoices are open?
question_template: Which customers still have open invoices but haven't paid anything in the last 60 days, and how many invoices are open?

question: For each plane model, how many flights carried both dangerous goods and temperature-controlled cargo?
question_template: For each plane model, how many flights carried both dangerous goods and temperature-controlled cargo?
answer_spec: Columns: model, number of flights (any status) carrying at least one dangerous-goods shipment AND at least one temperature-controlled shipment; ordered by model.
gold_sql: SELECT t.model, COUNT(*) AS mixed_flights FROM flights f JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = f.aircraft_id JOIN aircraft_types t ON t.type_id = a.type_id WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM flight_cargo fc JOIN shipments s ON s.shipment_id = fc.shipment_id WHERE fc.flight_id = f.flight_id AND s.is_dangerous_goods = 1) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM flight_cargo fc JOIN shipments s ON s.shipment_id = fc.shipment_id WHERE fc.flight_id = f.flight_id AND s.is_temperature_controlled = 1) GROUP BY t.type_id, t.model ORDER BY t.model

question: Among customers with at least 20 shipments, which 5 book most often, measured by average days between bookings?
question_template: Among customers with at least 20 shipments, which 5 book most often, measured by average days between bookings?

question: Which planes flew more hours than the average plane of their own airline?
question_template: Which planes flew more hours than the average plane of their own airline?
answer_spec: Columns: airline name, tail_number, completed block hours (rounded 1) of aircraft whose completed block hours exceed the average of their airline's flying aircraft; ordered by airline name, hours DESC.
gold_sql: WITH h AS ( SELECT a.airline_id, a.tail_number, SUM((julianday(f.actual_arrival) - julianday(f.actual_departure)) * 24) AS hours FROM flights f JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = f.aircraft_id WHERE f.status = 'completed' GROUP BY a.aircraft_id, a.airline_id, a.tail_number ), avg_h AS (SELECT airline_id, AVG(hours) AS avg_hours FROM h GROUP BY airline_id) SELECT al.name AS airline_name, h.tail_number, ROUND(h.hours, 1) AS block_hours FROM h JOIN avg_h ON avg_h.airline_id = h.airline_id JOIN airlines al ON al.airline_id = h.airline_id WHERE h.hours > avg_h.avg_hours ORDER BY airline_name, block_hours DESC

question: Which 5 routes with at least 10 loaded completed flights have the highest average load by weight?
question_template: Which 5 routes with at least 10 loaded completed flights have the highest average load by weight?
answer_spec: Columns: origin iata, destination iata, flights, average payload load factor in percent (cargo kg on the flight / max_payload_kg * 100, rounded 1) over completed flights carrying cargo; routes with at least 10 such flights; top 5 by load factor.
gold_sql: WITH l AS ( SELECT fc.flight_id, SUM(s.total_weight_kg) AS kg FROM flight_cargo fc JOIN shipments s ON s.shipment_id = fc.shipment_id GROUP BY fc.flight_id ) SELECT o.iata_code AS origin, d.iata_code AS destination, COUNT(*) AS flights, ROUND(AVG(l.kg * 100.0 / t.max_payload_kg), 1) AS avg_load_factor_pct FROM l JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id = l.flight_id AND f.status = 'completed' JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = f.aircraft_id JOIN aircraft_types t ON t.type_id = a.type_id JOIN airports o ON o.airport_id = f.origin_airport_id JOIN airports d ON d.airport_id = f.destination_airport_id GROUP BY o.iata_code, d.iata_code HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10 ORDER BY avg_load_factor_pct DESC, origin, destination LIMIT 5

gold_sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS incidents, ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN ic.status IN ('approved', 'paid') THEN ic.approved_amount_usd END), 0), 2) AS approved_usd FROM incidents i JOIN flight_cargo fc ON fc.flight_cargo_id = i.flight_cargo_id JOIN shipments s ON s.shipment_id = fc.shipment_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id LEFT JOIN insurance_claims ic ON ic.incident_id = i.incident_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4 ORDER BY incidents DESC, c.customer_id

question: For each airline, how often did a flight leave over an hour late right after the same plane's previous flight arrived over an hour late?
question_template: For each airline, how often did a flight leave over an hour late right after the same plane's previous flight arrived over an hour late?
answer_spec: Columns: airline name, number of completed flights departing more than 60 minutes late whose aircraft's previous completed flight arrived more than 60 minutes late; ordered by count DESC, name.
gold_sql: WITH s AS ( SELECT f.aircraft_id, (julianday(f.actual_departure) - julianday(f.scheduled_departure)) * 1440 AS dep_delay, LAG((julianday(f.actual_arrival) - julianday(f.scheduled_arrival)) * 1440) OVER (PARTITION BY f.aircraft_id ORDER BY f.actual_departure) AS prev_arr_delay FROM flights f WHERE f.status = 'completed' ) SELECT al.name AS airline_name, COUNT(*) AS knock_on_delays FROM s JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = s.aircraft_id JOIN airlines al ON al.airline_id = a.airline_id WHERE s.dep_delay > 60 AND s.prev_arr_delay > 60 GROUP BY al.airline_id, al.name ORDER BY knock_on_delays DESC, airline_name

question: Which 5 active planes have gone the longest since their last finished maintenance?
question_template: Which 5 active planes have gone the longest since their last finished maintenance?
answer_spec: Columns: tail_number, end of its latest completed maintenance, days from that end to 2025-12-20 (integer); active aircraft only; the 5 with the most days, ties by tail_number.

question: Which 5 airports have the most expensive fuel, and how much above the network average is it?
question_template: Which 5 airports have the most expensive fuel, and how much above the network average is it?
answer_spec: Columns: iata_code, average fuel price per litre at that airport (rounded 4), difference from the average price over all uplifts (rounded 4); the 5 most expensive airports.

question: At which airports did export customs clear less than 2 hours before the plane actually left?
question_template: At which airports did export customs clear less than 2 hours before the plane actually left?
answer_spec: Columns: origin iata_code, number of cleared export declarations cleared less than 2 hours before the shipment's leg-1 actual departure; airports with none omitted; ordered by count DESC, iata_code.
gold_sql: SELECT a.iata_code, COUNT(*) AS last_minute_clearances FROM customs_declarations d JOIN flight_cargo fc ON fc.shipment_id = d.shipment_id AND fc.leg_number = 1 JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id = fc.flight_id JOIN airports a ON a.airport_id = f.origin_airport_id WHERE d.declaration_type = 'export' AND d.status = 'cleared' AND f.status = 'completed' AND (julianday(f.actual_departure) - julianday(d.cleared_at)) * 24 < 2 GROUP BY a.airport_id, a.iata_code ORDER BY last_minute_clearances DESC, a.iata_code

gold_sql: WITH c AS ( SELECT s.customer_id, a.iata_code, COUNT(*) AS n FROM shipments s JOIN airports a ON a.airport_id = s.destination_airport_id WHERE s.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY s.customer_id, a.iata_code ), r AS ( SELECT c.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY n DESC, iata_code) AS rn, SUM(n) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) AS total FROM c ) SELECT cu.name, r.iata_code AS top_destination, r.n AS shipments FROM r JOIN customers cu ON cu.customer_id = r.customer_id WHERE r.rn = 1 AND r.total >= 60 ORDER BY r.customer_id

question: For invoices paid in exactly two payments, how many days are there between the two, by type of customer?
question_template: For invoices paid in exactly two payments, how many days are there between the two, by type of customer?
answer_spec: Columns: customer_type, invoices paid in exactly two payments, average days between the first and second payment (rounded 1); ordered by customer_type.
gold_sql: WITH two AS ( SELECT invoice_id, MIN(payment_date) AS first_pay, MAX(payment_date) AS second_pay FROM payments GROUP BY invoice_id HAVING COUNT(*) = 2 ) SELECT c.customer_type, COUNT(*) AS two_part_invoices, ROUND(AVG(julianday(t.second_pay) - julianday(t.first_pay)), 1) AS avg_days_between FROM two t JOIN invoices i ON i.invoice_id = t.invoice_id JOIN shipments s ON s.shipment_id = i.shipment_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_type ORDER BY c.customer_type

question: In each sales region, which customer have we invoiced the most, and how much?
question_template: In each sales region, which customer have we invoiced the most, and how much?

question: Which five planes went the longest between two maintenance jobs, and how many days was that?
question_template: Which five planes went the longest between two maintenance jobs, and how many days was that?

question: Which customers did we invoice more than 1.5 times as much in the second half of 2025 as in the first half?
question_template: Which customers did we invoice more than 1.5 times as much in the second half of 2025 as in the first half?
answer_spec: Columns: customer name, invoiced USD in H1 2025 (issued Jan-Jun), in H2 2025 (Jul-Dec), both rounded 2; customers whose H2 amount is more than 1.5 times the H1 amount; ordered by name.
gold_sql: SELECT c.name, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN i.issued_date < '2025-07-01' THEN i.amount_usd ELSE 0 END), 2) AS h1_usd, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN i.issued_date >= '2025-07-01' THEN i.amount_usd ELSE 0 END), 2) AS h2_usd FROM invoices i JOIN shipments s ON s.shipment_id = i.shipment_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id WHERE i.issued_date >= '2025-01-01' AND i.issued_date < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN i.issued_date >= '2025-07-01' THEN i.amount_usd ELSE 0 END) > 1.5 * SUM(CASE WHEN i.issued_date < '2025-07-01' THEN i.amount_usd ELSE 0 END) ORDER BY c.name

question_template: Which five customers owe us the most on invoices that aren't fully paid?
answer_spec: Columns: customer name, open balance in USD = invoice amount minus payments received, summed over its invoices with status 'unpaid' or 'partially_paid' (rounded 2); the 5 customers with the largest open balance.
gold_sql: WITH paid AS ( SELECT invoice_id, SUM(amount_usd) AS paid_usd FROM payments GROUP BY invoice_id ) SELECT c.name, ROUND(SUM(i.amount_usd - COALESCE(p.paid_usd, 0)), 2) AS open_balance_usd FROM invoices i LEFT JOIN paid p ON p.invoice_id = i.invoice_id JOIN shipments s ON s.shipment_id = i.shipment_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id WHERE i.status IN ('unpaid', 'partially_paid') GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name ORDER BY open_balance_usd DESC LIMIT 5

question: For each aircraft model, how many completed flights flew with no cargo at all, and what share is that?
question_template: For each aircraft model, how many completed flights flew with no cargo at all, and what share is that?
answer_spec: Columns: model, completed flights, completed flights without any shipment leg, share of such empty flights in percent (rounded 1); ordered by model.
gold_sql: SELECT t.model, COUNT(*) AS completed_flights, SUM(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM flight_cargo fc WHERE fc.flight_id = f.flight_id) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS empty_flights, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM flight_cargo fc WHERE fc.flight_id = f.flight_id) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS empty_pct FROM flights f JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = f.aircraft_id JOIN aircraft_types t ON t.type_id = a.type_id WHERE f.status = 'completed' GROUP BY t.type_id, t.model ORDER BY t.model

question: After an AOG repair, how many hours does it take before the plane flies again, by airline?
question_template: After an AOG repair, how many hours does it take before the plane flies again, by airline?
answer_spec: Columns: airline name, AOG maintenance events (completed, is_aog = 1) followed by a completed flight of the same aircraft, average hours from the maintenance end_time to that aircraft's first completed departure after it (rounded 1); ordered by airline name.
gold_sql: WITH r AS ( SELECT a.airline_id, (SELECT MIN(f.actual_departure) FROM flights f WHERE f.aircraft_id = m.aircraft_id AND f.status = 'completed' AND f.actual_departure >= m.end_time) AS next_departure, m.end_time FROM maintenance_records m JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = m.aircraft_id WHERE m.is_aog = 1 AND m.status = 'completed' ) SELECT al.name AS airline_name, COUNT(*) AS aog_events, ROUND(AVG((julianday(next_departure) - julianday(end_time)) * 24), 1) AS avg_hours_to_next_departure FROM r JOIN airlines al ON al.airline_id = r.airline_id WHERE next_departure IS NOT NULL GROUP BY al.airline_id, al.name ORDER BY airline_name

gold_sql: WITH r AS ( SELECT a.airline_id, (SELECT MIN(f.actual_departure) FROM flights f WHERE f.aircraft_id = m.aircraft_id AND f.status = 'completed' AND f.actual_departure >= m.end_time) AS next_departure, m.end_time FROM maintenance_records m JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = m.aircraft_id WHERE m.is_aog = 1 AND m.status = 'completed' ) SELECT al.name AS airline_name, COUNT(*) AS aog_events, ROUND(AVG((julianday(next_departure) - julianday(end_time)) * 24), 1) AS avg_hours_to_next_departure FROM r JOIN airlines al ON al.airline_id = r.airline_id WHERE next_departure IS NOT NULL GROUP BY al.airline_id, al.name ORDER BY airline_name

question: Which pilots with at least 20 completed duties are pilot flying less than 35% of the time?

question: How do our unpaid invoices age as of 20 December 2025: not due, 1-30, 31-60 and over 60 days late?
question_template: How do our unpaid invoices age as of 20 December 2025: not due, 1-30, 31-60 and over 60 days late?
answer_spec: Columns: ageing bucket of invoices with status not 'paid' by days past due_date on 2025-12-20 ('not due', '1-30', '31-60', '61+'), number of invoices, SUM(amount_usd) rounded 2; ordered by the bucket order above.
gold_sql: WITH b AS ( SELECT amount_usd, CASE WHEN julianday('2025-12-20') - julianday(due_date) <= 0 THEN 'not due' WHEN julianday('2025-12-20') - julianday(due_date) <= 30 THEN '1-30' WHEN julianday('2025-12-20') - julianday(due_date) <= 60 THEN '31-60' ELSE '61+' END AS bucket FROM invoices WHERE status <> 'paid' ) SELECT bucket, COUNT(*) AS invoices, ROUND(SUM(amount_usd), 2) AS amount_usd FROM b GROUP BY bucket ORDER BY CASE bucket WHEN 'not due' THEN 0 WHEN '1-30' THEN 1 WHEN '31-60' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END

question_template: Among customers with at least 30 payments, which five pay late most often?
answer_spec: Columns: customer name, payments, share of payments made after the invoice's due_date in percent (rounded 1); customers with at least 30 payments; the 5 with the highest late share.
gold_sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS payments, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_date > i.due_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS late_pct FROM payments p JOIN invoices i ON i.invoice_id = p.invoice_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 30 ORDER BY 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.payment_date > i.due_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 5

question: Which captains have flown with at least 11 different first officers?
question_template: Which captains have flown with at least 11 different first officers?
answer_spec: Columns: captain employee_number, number of different first officers flown with (completed assignments, roles captain and first_officer on the same flight); captains with at least 11; ordered by count DESC, employee_number.
gold_sql: SELECT m.employee_number, COUNT(DISTINCT fo.crew_member_id) AS distinct_first_officers FROM crew_assignments cp JOIN crew_assignments fo ON fo.flight_id = cp.flight_id AND fo.duty_role = 'first_officer' AND fo.assignment_status = 'completed' JOIN crew_members m ON m.crew_member_id = cp.crew_member_id WHERE cp.duty_role = 'captain' AND cp.assignment_status = 'completed' GROUP BY m.crew_member_id, m.employee_number HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fo.crew_member_id) >= 11 ORDER BY distinct_first_officers DESC, m.employee_number

question: Which airports have worse average arrival delays than the network as a whole?
question_template: Which airports have worse average arrival delays than the network as a whole?
answer_spec: Columns: destination iata_code, average arrival delay in minutes of completed flights there (rounded 1); only airports whose average is above the average over all completed flights; ordered by delay DESC.
gold_sql: SELECT ap.iata_code, ROUND(AVG((julianday(f.actual_arrival) - julianday(f.scheduled_arrival)) * 1440), 1) AS avg_arrival_delay_min FROM flights f JOIN airports ap ON ap.airport_id = f.destination_airport_id WHERE f.status = 'completed' GROUP BY ap.airport_id, ap.iata_code HAVING AVG((julianday(f.actual_arrival) - julianday(f.scheduled_arrival)) * 1440) > (SELECT AVG((julianday(actual_arrival) - julianday(scheduled_arrival)) * 1440) FROM flights WHERE status = 'completed') ORDER BY avg_arrival_delay_min DESC

question: Which five planes fly the most hours per day they're in use?
question_template: Which five planes fly the most hours per day they're in use?
answer_spec: Columns: tail_number, completed block hours per day flown = SUM(actual arrival - actual departure in hours) / number of distinct actual_departure dates (rounded 2); the 5 highest.

question: When both customs clearances go through, how many hours pass between export and import clearance, by import country?

question: In each sales region, who are the top two customers by number of shipments (ties count together)?
question_template: In each sales region, who are the top two customers by number of shipments (ties count together)?
answer_spec: Columns: sales_region, customer name, non-cancelled shipments, dense rank within the region: customers ranked 1 to 2 by shipments in their sales region (ties share a rank); ordered by region, rank, name.
gold_sql: WITH c AS ( SELECT cu.sales_region, cu.name, COUNT(*) AS shipments FROM shipments s JOIN customers cu ON cu.customer_id = s.customer_id WHERE s.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY cu.customer_id, cu.sales_region, cu.name ), r AS ( SELECT c.*, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sales_region ORDER BY shipments DESC) AS region_rank FROM c ) SELECT sales_region, name, shipments, region_rank FROM r WHERE region_rank <= 2 ORDER BY sales_region, region_rank, name

answer_spec: Columns: sales_region, customer name, non-cancelled shipments, dense rank within the region: customers ranked 1 to 2 by shipments in their sales region (ties share a rank); ordered by region, rank, name.
gold_sql: WITH c AS ( SELECT cu.sales_region, cu.name, COUNT(*) AS shipments FROM shipments s JOIN customers cu ON cu.customer_id = s.customer_id WHERE s.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY cu.customer_id, cu.sales_region, cu.name ), r AS ( SELECT c.*, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sales_region ORDER BY shipments DESC) AS region_rank FROM c ) SELECT sales_region, name, shipments, region_rank FROM r WHERE region_rank <= 2 ORDER BY sales_region, region_rank, name

question: Which day of the week has the worst departure delays?
question_template: Which day of the week has the worst departure delays?
answer_spec: Columns: weekday number of scheduled_departure (0 = Sunday ... 6 = Saturday), completed flights, average departure delay in minutes (rounded 1); ordered by weekday number.
gold_sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%w', scheduled_departure) AS INTEGER) AS weekday, COUNT(*) AS completed_flights, ROUND(AVG((julianday(actual_departure) - julianday(scheduled_departure)) * 1440), 1) AS avg_departure_delay_min FROM flights WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%w', scheduled_departure) AS INTEGER) ORDER BY weekday

question: For each airline, how many completed flights carried cargo for three or more different customers?
question_template: For each airline, how many completed flights carried cargo for three or more different customers?
answer_spec: Columns: airline name, completed flights carrying shipments of at least 3 different customers; ordered by count DESC, name.
gold_sql: WITH m AS ( SELECT fc.flight_id FROM flight_cargo fc JOIN shipments s ON s.shipment_id = fc.shipment_id GROUP BY fc.flight_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_id) >= 3 ) SELECT al.name AS airline_name, COUNT(*) AS multi_customer_flights FROM m JOIN flights f ON f.flight_id = m.flight_id JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = f.aircraft_id JOIN airlines al ON al.airline_id = a.airline_id WHERE f.status = 'completed' GROUP BY al.airline_id, al.name ORDER BY multi_customer_flights DESC, airline_name

question: If we split customers into five equal groups by revenue, how much does each group bring in and what share is that?
question_template: If we split customers into five equal groups by revenue, how much does each group bring in and what share is that?
answer_spec: Columns: revenue quintile (NTILE(5) over customers by invoiced USD DESC, ties by customer_id; 1 = top), customers in it, invoiced USD (rounded 2), share of all invoiced revenue in percent (rounded 1); ordered by quintile.
gold_sql: WITH r AS ( SELECT s.customer_id, SUM(i.amount_usd) AS revenue FROM invoices i JOIN shipments s ON s.shipment_id = i.shipment_id GROUP BY s.customer_id ), q AS ( SELECT r.*, NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC, customer_id) AS quintile FROM r ) SELECT quintile, COUNT(*) AS customers, ROUND(SUM(revenue), 2) AS invoiced_usd, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(revenue) / (SELECT SUM(revenue) FROM r), 1) AS share_pct FROM q GROUP BY quintile ORDER BY quintile

question: Which airports send out temperature-controlled shipments without having a cold-chain warehouse, and how many?
question_template: Which airports send out temperature-controlled shipments without having a cold-chain warehouse, and how many?
answer_spec: Columns: origin iata_code, temperature-controlled shipments (any status) originating there; only airports without any 'cold_chain' warehouse; ordered by count DESC, iata_code.
gold_sql: SELECT ap.iata_code, COUNT(*) AS temp_controlled_shipments FROM shipments s JOIN airports ap ON ap.airport_id = s.origin_airport_id WHERE s.is_temperature_controlled = 1 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM warehouses w WHERE w.airport_id = ap.airport_id AND w.warehouse_type = 'cold_chain') GROUP BY ap.airport_id, ap.iata_code ORDER BY temp_controlled_shipments DESC, ap.iata_code

question: How many flights were cancelled because of weather in each month of 2025, including months with none?
question_template: How many flights were cancelled because of weather in each month of 2025, including months with none?
answer_spec: Columns: every month '2025-01' to '2025-12', number of flights with cancellation_reason 'weather' scheduled that month (0 when none); ordered by month.
gold_sql: WITH RECURSIVE months(m) AS ( SELECT '2025-01-01' UNION ALL SELECT date(m, '+1 month') FROM months WHERE m < '2025-12-01' ) SELECT substr(months.m, 1, 7) AS month, COUNT(f.flight_id) AS weather_cancellations FROM months LEFT JOIN flights f ON substr(f.scheduled_departure, 1, 7) = substr(months.m, 1, 7) AND f.cancellation_reason = 'weather' GROUP BY months.m ORDER BY month

question: Which planes flew on three or more days in a row, and what's their longest streak?
question_template: Which planes flew on three or more days in a row, and what's their longest streak?
answer_spec: Columns: tail_number, longest run of consecutive calendar days with at least one completed departure (by date of actual_departure); aircraft with a run of at least 3 days; ordered by run DESC, tail_number.
gold_sql: WITH d AS ( SELECT DISTINCT aircraft_id, date(actual_departure) AS day FROM flights WHERE status = 'completed' ), g AS ( SELECT aircraft_id, day, julianday(day) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY aircraft_id ORDER BY day) AS grp FROM d ), runs AS ( SELECT aircraft_id, grp, COUNT(*) AS run_days FROM g GROUP BY aircraft_id, grp ) SELECT a.tail_number, MAX(r.run_days) AS longest_run_days FROM runs r JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = r.aircraft_id GROUP BY a.aircraft_id, a.tail_number HAVING MAX(r.run_days) >= 3 ORDER BY longest_run_days DESC, a.tail_number

gold_sql: SELECT severity, COUNT(*) AS resolved_incidents, ROUND(AVG(julianday(resolved_at) - julianday(reported_at)), 1) AS avg_days_to_resolve, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN julianday(resolved_at) - julianday(reported_at) <= 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS within_30d_pct FROM incidents WHERE resolved = 1 GROUP BY severity ORDER BY severity

question: For each commodity, which invoiced shipment earned the most per chargeable kilo?
question_template: For each commodity, which invoiced shipment earned the most per chargeable kilo?
answer_spec: Columns: commodity_category, awb_number, invoice USD per chargeable kg (amount_usd / chargeable_weight_kg, rounded 2): per category the invoiced shipment with the highest yield (ties: smaller shipment_id); ordered by category.
gold_sql: WITH y AS ( SELECT s.commodity_category, s.awb_number, s.shipment_id, i.amount_usd / s.chargeable_weight_kg AS usd_per_kg FROM invoices i JOIN shipments s ON s.shipment_id = i.shipment_id ), r AS ( SELECT y.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY commodity_category ORDER BY usd_per_kg DESC, shipment_id) AS rn FROM y ) SELECT commodity_category, awb_number, ROUND(usd_per_kg, 2) AS usd_per_chargeable_kg FROM r WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY commodity_category

question: In each month of Q4 2025, what share of completed flights did each airline operate?
question_template: In each month of Q4 2025, what share of completed flights did each airline operate?
answer_spec: Columns: month 'YYYY-MM' (Oct-Dec 2025, by actual_departure), airline name, completed flights, share of that month's completed flights in percent (rounded 1); ordered by month, flights DESC, airline name.
gold_sql: WITH c AS ( SELECT substr(f.actual_departure, 1, 7) AS month, a.airline_id, COUNT(*) AS flights FROM flights f JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = f.aircraft_id WHERE f.status = 'completed' AND f.actual_departure >= '2025-10-01' AND f.actual_departure < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY substr(f.actual_departure, 1, 7), a.airline_id ) SELECT c.month, al.name AS airline_name, c.flights, ROUND(100.0 * c.flights / SUM(c.flights) OVER (PARTITION BY c.month), 1) AS share_pct FROM c JOIN airlines al ON al.airline_id = c.airline_id ORDER BY c.month, c.flights DESC, airline_name

question: For two-leg shipments, how often does the second leg go on a different airline, by first-leg airline?
question_template: For two-leg shipments, how often does the second leg go on a different airline, by first-leg airline?
answer_spec: Columns: airline name of leg 1, number of two-leg shipments whose leg 2 is flown by a different airline (interline); ordered by count DESC, name.
gold_sql: SELECT al.name AS first_leg_airline, COUNT(*) AS interline_shipments FROM flight_cargo l1 JOIN flight_cargo l2 ON l2.shipment_id = l1.shipment_id AND l2.leg_number = 2 JOIN flights f1 ON f1.flight_id = l1.flight_id JOIN aircraft a1 ON a1.aircraft_id = f1.aircraft_id JOIN flights f2 ON f2.flight_id = l2.flight_id JOIN aircraft a2 ON a2.aircraft_id = f2.aircraft_id JOIN airlines al ON al.airline_id = a1.airline_id WHERE l1.leg_number = 1 AND a1.airline_id <> a2.airline_id GROUP BY al.airline_id, al.name ORDER BY interline_shipments DESC, first_leg_airline
